verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is stalling, not erroring. Its logs show PlaceOrder entry lines continuing at normal cadence through 14:24:33 while the payment, confirmation-email and queue-write completion lines that followed every order earlier vanish from ~14:21:22 onward [tr_c7bb7669feb9], and its aggregate error ratio fell to roughly 43% of baseline with no threshold breach [tr_6165d2b75628]. Requests that start, never complete, and never carry an error status are the signature of a synchronous downstream call that hangs rather than fails. cartservice and productcatalogservice are both healthy in the observed evidence [tr_07ca09e8b4d2][tr_96ce5f7c3658], and no change landed on checkoutservice at all [tr_aa8840893bee] while every cartservice mutation was reverted well before onset [tr_183ded784091]. The best-supported verdict is that a dependency in checkout's post-intake path (payment, email, or the order-queue write) became slow, and checkoutservice's downstream fan-out — accounting, email, fraud-detection, quote all alerting together at 14:22:45 — reflects orders never reaching those stages. checkoutservice is named because it is where the stall is observed and where request completion breaks, but the failing dependency itself was never measured.
verdict.reasoning: The only positive signal anywhere on the board is the log discontinuity in checkoutservice: intake continues, completion stops, no errors, no status codes, no crash or panic lines [tr_c7bb7669feb9]. Error-ratio metrics rule out hard-failure propagation from any downstream returning errors [tr_6165d2b75628] and rule out productcatalogservice as an error source [tr_96ce5f7c3658]; latency-only degradation is explicitly left open by both. cartservice's change history is a red herring — image, REDIS_ADDR and 300ms latency-injection mutations all recur but every one is reverted 1.6-2.2h before onset [tr_183ded784091] — and its own logs show no stall or Redis failure in the observed tail [tr_07ca09e8b4d2]. With no checkoutservice change record [tr_aa8840893bee], deploy and config mechanisms have nothing to point at, leaving waiting-on-a-slow-dependency as the mechanism the evidence best fits.
open_questions: Which dependency is actually slow: no latency percentiles, trace spans, or per-downstream breakdown were ever collected for checkoutservice, paymentservice, emailservice, or the order queue.

cartservice logs are truncated across 12:49:38-14:24:19, so the entire onset interval is unobserved, and its error-ratio series is absent in both windows [tr_6de53147ad78] — cartservice is unexcluded, not cleared.
Whether the recurring platform-automation latency-injection cycle on cartservice fired again inside the unqueried onset window, or landed on a service whose change log was never pulled.
What signal the 14:19:30 checkoutservice alert actually fired on, since it was not error ratio [tr_6165d2b75628].

alternatives.root_cause: A recurring automated 300ms traffic-shaping fault injection re-attached to cartservice (or a peer) near onset, slowing checkout's cart calls.
alternatives.why_not: The change log shows the last injection removed 1.8h before onset with no re-attachment in the window [tr_183ded784091], and cartservice's observed tail shows millisecond intra-request gaps with no stall [tr_07ca09e8b4d2]. Only the truncated log middle keeps it alive.

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice exhausted a bounded resource — connection pool, worker threads, or outbound sockets — so orders queue at intake and never reach the payment stage.
alternatives.why_not: No saturation, memory, CPU, thread or connection-pool metric was ever queried, so this is unmeasured rather than supported; the same log pattern is equally consistent with waiting on a slow callee, which at least has a mechanism the error-ratio evidence corroborates.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log stream should be expected. The next observable step is diagnostic, not remedial: collect per-downstream latency percentiles or trace spans for checkoutservice's post-intake calls (paymentservice, emailservice, the order-queue write) covering 14:19:00-14:25:00, plus the alert definition that fired at 14:19:30. Those would show which span duration diverged, which is the fact no permitted action can be chosen without.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the stall is in fact resident in checkoutservice's own process state — for example an exhausted outbound connection pool or a leaked goroutine holding every worker — in which case a restart_service on checkoutservice would restore the payment/email/queue-write completion lines within a minute and the abstention will have cost that minute. The evidence available cannot distinguish that from a genuinely slow dependency: no latency percentiles, no per-downstream breakdown, no restart or resource-saturation signal for checkoutservice was ever collected [tr_6165d2b75628], and checkoutservice's own logs name no dependency and carry no error or status codes at all [tr_c7bb7669feb9]. It is also wrong if a latency injection fired inside the unqueried onset window on a service whose change log was never pulled — paymentservice, emailservice and currencyservice all have no change history in evidence — in which case the fix is a config_revert on that service, still not on checkoutservice.
proposal.risk: The risk being avoided is real, which is why abstaining is the answer rather than a formality. restart_service is the only action whose preconditions could be argued, and it fails them: the evidence points at a hung synchronous outbound call after intake [tr_c7bb7669feb9], not at process state, and it explicitly rules out crash, panic, and intake failure. Restarting checkoutservice is irreversible, would kill every in-flight PlaceOrder — the orders currently stalled between intake and payment would be destroyed rather than completed, turning a stall into lost transactions — and if the slow dependency is genuinely downstream the new container would stall identically within seconds, having spent the outage's only irreversible action for nothing. rollback_image and revert_config are barred outright: the change log for checkoutservice is empty across the full window [tr_aa8840893bee], so no prior image tag or configuration exists to restore and no change is named inside the window. scale_service is unavailable in this world. Acting on cartservice instead would be worse: every mutation there was reverted well before onset [tr_183ded784091], so a revert has nothing to restore, and cartservice is unexcluded only because its logs are truncated across the entire onset interval — absence of coverage, not a fault to fix.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. For contrast, the action not taken would have been felt: a checkoutservice restart resets connections for frontend, its inbound caller, and the stalled orders in flight would not reach accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice or quoteservice — the four services already alerting at 14:22:45 because orders never reach them. Those four plus shippingservice, reached via quoteservice, are the population whose recovery a wrong action would delay while the real dependency stayed slow.
proposal.target_note: Empty target is deliberate: the service where the stall is observed is not the service where the fault lives, and the failing dependency was never measured.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert on checkoutservice followed three minutes later by its four downstream consumers alerting simultaneously — a real fan-out failure that cannot be dismissed. The checkout-first ordering points upstream at checkout or one of its dependencies, but nothing in the alerts distinguishes a deploy, config, or dependency slowdown yet.
